description: Reference coefficients: clinical benefit per unit biomarker change. 'value_derived' = true when the value was computed from a percentage in the source (computation stated in note). Keep trial-scale (~5 y) and lifelong genetic scales separate.

effect.per_unit: 1.0 mmol/L (38.7 mg/dL) LDL-C reduction (achieved at 1 year)
effect.outcome: major vascular events (coronary death, non-fatal MI, coronary revascularisation, stroke)

entries.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)
measurement_pitfalls: Trial-scale (CTT, ~5 y) and lifelong genetic (MR) coefficients differ ~2-3x; Ference 2012 (R2) reports lifelong genetic effect per mmol/L is 3-fold greater than statin-trial effect. Never mix scales.

CETP inhibitors: R3 reports that a direct LDL-C assay underestimated on-treatment LDL-C with anacetrapib (REVEAL direct assay -41% vs beta-quantification -17%) and likely overestimated reduction with evacetrapib; use beta-quantification or apoB. (Brief said 'Friedewald'; the verified source names the direct assay.)
Measured 'LDL-C' includes Lp(a)-cholesterol (general caveat, not from a cited source here); large Lp(a) lowering can shift reported LDL-C.
Coefficient is per ABSOLUTE mmol/L reduction at 1 year (placebo-adjusted), not per % reduction; 1 mmol/L = 38.67 mg/dL (R8).
entries.note: Statin trials (26 RCTs, ~170,000 participants). All-cause mortality RR 0.90 (0.87-0.93) per 1.0 mmol/L (same abstract). Benchmark coefficient for the calculator.

entries.quote: the risk reduction was 22% (95% CI 20–24; p<0·0001) per 1·0 mmol/L reduction in LDL cholesterol at 1 year, with a significant 12% reduction during the first year after randomisation (p<0·0001) and highly significant reductions of about a quarter during each subsequent year (all p<0·0001; webappendix p 3 )
measurement_pitfalls: Trial-scale (CTT, ~5 y) and lifelong genetic (MR) coefficients differ ~2-3x; Ference 2012 (R2) reports lifelong genetic effect per mmol/L is 3-fold greater than statin-trial effect. Never mix scales.

(Brief said 'Friedewald'; the verified source names the direct assay.)
Measured 'LDL-C' includes Lp(a)-cholesterol (general caveat, not from a cited source here); large Lp(a) lowering can shift reported LDL-C.
Coefficient is per ABSOLUTE mmol/L reduction at 1 year (placebo-adjusted), not per % reduction; 1 mmol/L = 38.67 mg/dL (R8).
entries.note: Year-1 attenuation. Value 0.88 derived from '12% reduction'; CI not given in main text (webappendix p3, not read) -> ci null. Subsequent years: 'about a quarter' (~RR 0.75 per mmol/L, approximate, per-year table NOT FOUND in main text). Short trials (<2 y) should expect markedly less than 22% per mmol/L.

entries.quote: naturally random allocation to long-term exposure to lower LDL-C was associated with a 54.5% (95% confidence interval: 48.8% to 59.5%) reduction in the risk of CHD for each mmol/l (38.7 mg/dl) lower LDL-C. This represents a 3-fold greater reduction in the risk of CHD per unit lower LDL-C than that observed during treatment with a statin
measurement_pitfalls: Trial-scale (CTT, ~5 y) and lifelong genetic (MR) coefficients differ ~2-3x; Ference 2012 (R2) reports lifelong genetic effect per mmol/L is 3-fold greater than statin-trial effect. Never mix scales.

(Brief said 'Friedewald'; the verified source names the direct assay.)
Measured 'LDL-C' includes Lp(a)-cholesterol (general caveat, not from a cited source here); large Lp(a) lowering can shift reported LDL-C.
Coefficient is per ABSOLUTE mmol/L reduction at 1 year (placebo-adjusted), not per % reduction; 1 mmol/L = 38.67 mg/dL (R8).
entries.note: Value and CI derived as 1 - % reduction (0.455; 0.405-0.512). Measure in abstract is 'reduction in risk' (MR ratio). Use only for lifelong-scale comparisons, not to predict a 3-5 y trial.

effect.timescale: ~5 years in-trial (median 5.1 y pooled; REVEAL 4.6 y, IMPROVE-IT 6.1 y)
effect.outcome: major cardiovascular events (CV death, MI, ischemic stroke, coronary revascularization)

measurement_pitfalls: Both trials happened to have a 12 mg/dL apoB difference, so this is effectively a two-trial pooled RR at one dose, not a fitted slope; scaling to other apoB differences assumes log-linearity.
apoB difference defined as on-treatment active minus placebo (Table 2 footnote).
Source is a narrative review (R3), not a formal systematic meta-regression; number verified in its Table 2.
entries.note: Brief's figure verified exactly. Implies ~0.75 per 1 mmol/L-equivalent only under assumptions; use per-12 mg/dL as published.

entries.quote: a genetic score consisting of variants with naturally occurring discordance between levels of LDL-C and apoB was associated with a similar risk of CHD per unit change in apoB level (OR, 0.782 [95% CI, 0.720-0.845] vs 0.793 [95% CI, 0.774-0.812]; P = .79 for difference)
entries.location: Abstract; unit '10-mg/dL lower apoB' stated in Figure 2 legend and Results
measurement_pitfalls: Lifelong genetic scale: roughly 2-3x larger than in-trial effect per unit (compare R1/R2, R8 Table 2).
INTERNAL DISCREPANCY: main-text Results report the discordant score as 'OR, 0.772 [95% CI, 0.701-0.844]' and concordant as 0.788 (0.769-0.807), vs abstract 0.782/0.793.
entries.note: 0.782 is the discordant (LDL-C/apoB) score in external CARDIoGRAMplusC4D validation; the concordant LDL-C score gave 0.793 (0.774-0.812). Key point: risk tracks apoB, not LDL-C, when the two diverge (e.g., CETP inhibition).

effect.per_unit: 1 SD genetically HIGHER HDL-C (14-SNP genetic score)

entries.quote: a 1 SD increase in HDL cholesterol due to genetic score was not associated with risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·93, 95% CI 0·68-1·26, p=0·63)
measurement_pitfalls: Direction: per 1 SD INCREASE (raising), not reduction.

Observational estimate is strongly confounded: 'an increase of 1 SD in HDL cholesterol was associated with reduced risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·62, 95% CI 0·58-0·66)' (R7 abstract) - do not use as a causal coefficient.
HDL-C rise from CETP inhibitors should be assigned zero benefit; score such drugs on apoB/non-HDL-C instead.
entries.note: LIPG Asn396Ser: expected OR 0.87 (0.84-0.91) but observed 0.99 (0.88-1.11) (R7 abstract). Calculator coefficient for HDL-C raising = null effect (OR 1.0).

entries.quote: A 10-mg/dL lower genetically predicted Lp(a) concentration was associated with a 5.8% lower CHD risk (odds ratio [OR], 0.942; 95% CI, 0.933-0.951; P = 3 × 10-37)
measurement_pitfalls: UNITS: coefficient is per mg/dL (mass). EAS consensus (R9): 'This panel does not recommend using a standard factor to convert between mg/dL and nmol/L, as assays vary extensively.' 2-2.5 is only a 'best guess' (mg/dL to nmol/L). Trials of antisense/siRNA agents usually report nmol/L.
Benefit is proportional to ABSOLUTE reduction (R8); % reductions in low-baseline populations yield tiny absolute changes.
Equivalence: 101.5 mg/dL (95% CI 71.0-137.0) Lp(a) change ~ 38.67 mg/dL (1 mmol/L) LDL-C change (R8 abstract).
Lifelong vs trial scale differ ~2x (see next entry).
entries.note: Causal per genetics; as of these sources no completed outcome trial had confirmed benefit of Lp(a)-specific lowering (R9: 'Trials of specific Lp(a)-lowering treatments are critical to confirm clinical benefit').

effect.timescale: ~5 years in-trial (estimated by scaling to CTT statin effect)

entries.quote: Table 2. Expected Clinical Benefit of Lowering Lp(a) ... 100 38.1 (28.4-54.5) 44.9 (39.7-49.8) 23.7 (17.8-32.4)
entries.location: Table 2 (row 100 mg/dL: LDL-C-equivalent 38.1 mg/dL; lifelong RRR 44.9%; estimated short-term trial RRR 23.7%)
measurement_pitfalls: Same units pitfall as above (mg/dL, not nmol/L).
This is a model-based projection (MR estimate rescaled with CTT ~5-y statin data), not observed trial data.
entries.note: Value/CI derived as 1 - short-term RRR (23.7%, 17.8-32.4). Other rows of R8 Table 2: 50 mg/dL -> 12.6% (9.3-17.8); 30 mg/dL -> 7.8% (5.7-11.1). Lifelong RRR for 100 mg/dL is 44.9% vs 23.7% short-term (~1.9x).

entries.quote: Causal risk ratios for coronary heart disease per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity were: 0.95 (0.88-1.03) with Val279Phe; 0.92 (0.74-1.16) with carriage of any loss-of-function variant; 1.01 (0.68-1.51) with Val379Ala; and 0.95 (0.89-1.02) with darapladib treatment.
measurement_pitfalls: Coefficient is per % lower enzyme ACTIVITY (65% = darapladib 160 mg effect), not per mass concentration.
Observational Lp-PLA2 associations are confounded (marker travels with LDL particles).
entries.note: Darapladib trials gave a concordant null: 0.95 (0.89-1.02) per 65% lower activity.

entries.quote: the OR derived from the genetic instrumental variable analysis for MVE for a 1-log unit lower sPLA2-IIA mass was 1.04 (95% CI: 0.96 to 1.13), and differed from the non-genetic observational estimate (OR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.61 to 0.79)
measurement_pitfalls: Instrument (PLA2G2A rs11573156) lowers sPLA2-IIA mass 38-44% but enzyme activity only 3-23% per allele; mass and activity are not interchangeable.
Observational OR 0.69 (0.61-0.79) is confounded; do not use.
entries.note: Varespladib phase III stopped for lack of efficacy (R11 background). ACS cohorts also null: per-allele OR 0.96 (0.90-1.03).

entries.quote: the RR per 1-mmol/L reduction in non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol was 0.79 (95% CI, 0.76-0.82; P<0.0001; 0.78 per 40 mg/dL)
measurement_pitfalls: 1 mmol/L non-HDL-C = 38.67 mg/dL; R6 reports per 40 mg/dL separately (0.78).
non-HDL-C includes Lp(a)-C and remnant-C; with CETP inhibitors non-HDL-C/apoB is preferred to directly measured LDL-C (R3).
Trial-level meta-regression (49 trials, 374,358 participants) - ecological; dominated by statin trials.
entries.note: CTT 2010 (R1) does not report a non-HDL-C coefficient in its abstract; Marston 2019 used instead.

entries.quote: Every 10 mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure significantly reduced the risk of major cardiovascular disease events (relative risk [RR] 0·80, 95% CI 0·77-0·83)
measurement_pitfalls: Office SBP in trials; achieved between-arm difference (not % change).
Smaller proportional reductions in diabetes and CKD (R12 abstract); beta-blockers inferior for MACE/stroke.
entries.note: Abstract-only access (Lancet paywalled).

effect.per_unit: 5 mmHg SBP reduction (participants WITHOUT prior CVD)
effect.outcome: major cardiovascular event (stroke, MI/IHD, HF death or hospitalisation)

entries.quote: Hazard ratios (HR) associated with a reduction of systolic blood pressure by 5 mm Hg for a major cardiovascular event were 0·91, 95% CI 0·89-0·94 for partipants without previous cardiovascular disease and 0·89, 0·86-0·92, for those with previous cardiovascular disease.
measurement_pitfalls: Per 5 mmHg, not 10; squaring gives ~0.83/0.79 per 10 mmHg (approximation).
IPD from 48 RCTs; effect proportional to SBP reduction irrespective of baseline SBP.
entries.note: Quote contains original typo 'partipants'.

effect.per_unit: 5 mmHg SBP reduction (participants WITH prior CVD)

entries.quote: 0·89, 0·86-0·92, for those with previous cardiovascular disease
measurement_pitfalls: Per 5 mmHg.
entries.note: Secondary-prevention counterpart of the entry above.

effect.per_unit: 10 mg/dL lower apoB-containing lipoproteins via LPL variants (~69.9 mg/dL lower triglycerides)

entries.quote: the LPL and LDLR scores were associated with similar lower risk of CHD per 10-mg/dL lower level of ApoB-containing lipoproteins (OR, 0.771 [95% CI, 0.741-0.802], P = 3.9 × 10-38 and OR, 0.773 [95% CI, 0.747-0.801], P = 1.1 × 10-46, respectively)
measurement_pitfalls: Triglyceride benefit is mediated by apoB: per 10 mg/dL apoB the LPL score lowered TG by 69.9 mg/dL (68.1-71.6) vs LDLR score lowering LDL-C by 14.2 mg/dL (R5 abstract). Score TG drugs on apoB change, not TG change.
After adjusting for apoB in multivariable MR: TG OR 1.014 (0.965-1.065), LDL-C OR 1.010 (0.967-1.055), apoB OR 0.761 (0.723-0.798) (R5 abstract).
R5 full text: fibrate trials lowered TG only 20-50 mg/dL, 'a fraction of what would be needed to significantly reduce the risk of major vascular events within a short-term trial'.
Lifelong genetic scale.
entries.note: TG per se not independently causal once apoB accounted for; benefit of large TG lowering ~ apoB-equivalent. REDUCE-IT/JELIS benefit exceeded lipid-predicted effect (R5 discussion).

effect.per_unit: 1 mmol/L TG reduction, adjusted for LDL-C (0.92 per 40 mg/dL)

entries.quote: the RR was 0.80 (95% CI, 0.76-0.85; P<0.0001) per 1-mmol/L (0.79 per 40 mg/dL) reduction in LDL-C and 0.84 (95% CI, 0.75-0.94; P=0.0026) per 1-mmol/L (0.92 per 40 mg/dL) reduction in triglycerides
measurement_pitfalls: Strongly driven by REDUCE-IT; excluding it: 0.91 (0.81-1.006) per 1 mmol/L TG (R6 abstract).
1 mmol/L TG = 88.5 mg/dL (standard conversion).
Omega-3 EPA benefit appears to exceed lipid effects (R6).
entries.note: Marked uncertain: trial-level TG coefficient is fragile and confounded by EPA non-lipid effects.

effect.per_unit: 1 SD higher genetically raised ln CRP

entries.quote: In a combined analysis, the risk ratio for coronary heart disease was 1.00 (0.90 to 1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised natural log (ln) concentration of C reactive protein.
measurement_pitfalls: Observational RR 1.33 (1.23-1.43) per 1 SD higher ln CRP (R14 abstract) is not causal.
CRP is a downstream marker: CRP lowering via IL-6 pathway may still mark benefit from upstream causal inflammation (see IL-6 entry); do not credit CRP lowering per se.
entries.note: Direction: per 1 SD HIGHER; null either way.

effect.per_unit: per copy of IL6R 358Ala minor allele (~7.5% lower CRP, 14.6% higher IL-6, 34.3% higher soluble IL6R)

entries.quote: The odds ratio per minor allele was 0·966 (95% CI 0·950–0·982, p=4·5×10 −5 ).
entries.location: Figure 2 legend (full text); abstract: 'risk of coronary heart disease was reduced by 3·4% (1·8-5·0)' per copy
measurement_pitfalls: Circulating IL-6 RISES with IL6R impairment (receptor blockade); IL-6 level is not a valid efficacy biomarker. Use CRP/fibrinogen as pathway readouts.
Per-allele coefficient, not per unit biomarker; scaling to drug effect (e.g., tocilizumab/ziltivekimab) requires CRP-based calibration (assumption).
entries.note: Pathway-level causal evidence. Replication (R16): rs7529229 'per allele odds ratio 0·95, 95% CI 0·93-0·97, p=1·53×10(-5)' in 25,458 cases/100,740 controls.

effect.per_unit: per IL6R rs7529229 allele (proxy for Asp358Ala; ~8.35% lower CRP per allele)

entries.quote: the IL6R rs7529229 SNP was associated with a decreased odds of coronary heart disease events (per allele odds ratio 0·95, 95% CI 0·93-0·97, p=1·53×10(-5))
measurement_pitfalls: Same as above: IL-6 concentration increases per allele (9.45%) while CRP falls (8.35%).
entries.note: Independent consortium replicating R15.

effect.outcome: coronary heart disease events (fatal + non-fatal MI)

entries.quote: The mean haemoglobin A(1c) concentration (HbA(1c)) was 0.9% lower for participants given intensive treatment than for those given standard treatment. Intensive glycaemic control resulted in a 17% reduction in events of non-fatal myocardial infarction (odds ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.93), and a 15% reduction in events of coronary heart disease (0.85, 0.77-0.93).
measurement_pitfalls: No effect on stroke 0.93 (0.81-1.06) or all-cause mortality 1.02 (0.87-1.19) (R17 abstract).

HbA1c difference is an average across heterogeneous regimens; drug-specific effects (hypoglycaemia, weight, non-glycaemic actions of SGLT2i/GLP-1RA) are not captured - do not attribute CVOT benefit of modern agents to HbA1c lowering (general caveat).
Single-dose comparison, not a fitted per-unit slope.
entries.note: Causal 'uncertain' for MACE: MI benefit modest, no mortality benefit, increased hypoglycaemia (R18).

effect.per_unit: more-intensive vs less-intensive glucose control (HbA1c difference NOT stated in abstract)

entries.quote: Allocation to more-intensive, compared with less-intensive, glucose control reduced the risk of major cardiovascular events by 9% (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.99), primarily because of a 15% reduced risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.76-0.94).
measurement_pitfalls: Per-unit HbA1c difference NOT FOUND in abstract (commonly cited ~0.88% is unverified here).
Major hypoglycaemia HR 2.48 (1.91-3.21); possible harm/no benefit in those with prior macrovascular disease (HR 1.00 vs 0.84, interaction p=0.04).
entries.note: MACE-level estimate for the glucose-lowering entry; per_unit unresolved.
